nodes.label: Multi-agent dependency graph
nodes.rationale: Independent agents run concurrently under a shared per-process limit; depends_on chains receive upstream output, and invalid graphs are rejected before any provider call.

nodes.label: Caller-owned conversation history
nodes.rationale: Histories and context are owned and persisted by the caller, not the module, so the module is not an authorization boundary and no context is silently truncated.

nodes.label: URL-prefix API versioning
nodes.rationale: Versioning in the URL prefix lets breaking changes ship as /api/v2 without disturbing existing /api/v1 clients.

nodes.label: Vite /api dev proxy
nodes.rationale: Keeps the browser on one origin in development so VITE_API_BASE_URL can stay relative; production instead sets the real API origin and enables CORS.

nodes.label: Hell week
nodes.rationale: Flags heavy stretches of the semester (default threshold 50 hours in a 7-day window, plus stress >= 7 events) so workload spikes are visible before they happen.

nodes.label: Layering rules
nodes.rationale: Keeps the layers honest: endpoints parse, services hold rules, repositories own SQL, components render, only src/api talks to fetch, so each request stays in one predictable shape.

nodes.label: GOOGLE_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY
nodes.rationale: Credential stays on the backend; it must never be placed in a VITE_ variable or frontend code.

nodes.label: No-authentication scaffold warning
nodes.rationale: CORS does not prevent API use, so the Gemma endpoints must be protected by the application's own authentication, authorization and quota before public deployment.
